Ingos

Setting

Ingos is nominally Canian, but its governor’s effective power scarcely extends beyond the city walls. Independent communities and Woodsfolk inhabit the surrounding snowlands. Kir and Kel arrive following the Magic Orb’s clue. Brissen’s murder, a staged caravan and conflicting alibis make their visit an investigation; the cleared magician Yam-Akara discovers the route to Jigran. [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

Two magicians on Ingos

Kir and Kel seek magical help on Ingos. Karansul complains about Yam-Akara, whose cheap runes undercut his trade, and identifies His as the governor’s court magician. His receives the travellers with suspicion and later asks them to retrieve materials from his laboratory. Sver the Trapper offers another route: contact Grey Leaf through the Sacred Flower and a vessel from his cache. Grey Leaf explains that the knight Brissen and his magician friend have left for the settlement near the mines. Kir’s first task here is finding an informed ally, before the murder that later dominates the investigation. [6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11]

The Beastmasters and the empty caravan

At the Beastmasters’ settlement, Crooked accuses Kir and Kel of being spies. Geraldine agrees to test them. Their attempt to obtain a gold nugget from a caravan finds an empty chest, making their return dangerous. Trickster reasons that genuine thieves would not come back empty-handed, and Geraldine accepts them. Sver’s advice about an ice elemental in the abandoned mines provides something to offer Yam-Akara. His work and the governor’s permit requirements then draw the travellers into further dealings with the court. The missing nugget will matter again when the apparent caravan failure becomes evidence of a separate theft. [12, 13, 14, 15, 3]

Brissen’s murder and the failed alibi

Brissen is murdered and Yam-Akara is accused of killing his old friend. Kir and Kel undertake the defence. The magician says he spent the day in the mines and arrived late for their meeting. Mine guard confirms that he allowed the elderly visitor through with an expired permit and stamped it that day. Kir finds the lost pass, but Valrasian rejects the water-damaged document because the signature and date can no longer be read. This evidence supports the search but does not free Yam-Akara; the travellers still have to identify the murderer. [16, 17, 18, 19, 20]

The planted knife and His’s death

A knife found at the murder site appears to implicate His. The court magician admits it was stolen from his laboratory together with the governor’s nugget. He had sent out the empty caravan to hide that loss and hoped to blame raiders after an informant warned of the planned attack. His arranges a meeting to produce evidence, but is killed before he can clear himself. Meanwhile Geraldine and Karansul disclose their relationship and provide each other with an alibi. Their commercial hostility and private secrecy had made them suspicious without establishing guilt. [21, 22, 3, 23, 24]

Crooked’s confession

The settlement’s missing communal money supplies the decisive motive. Kir and Kel catch Crooked at his cache. Brissen had discovered the theft, so Crooked killed him. He also stole His’s knife and the gold nugget, informed on the caravan raid and later planted the knife to shift suspicion. His called the same informant to clear his own name; Crooked mistook that invitation for a trap and killed him too. Woodsfolk observations help reconstruct the planted evidence. Before the governor, Kir explains the connected crimes and Crooked admits them. Yam-Akara is released, while the governor reserves Crooked’s punishment for trial. [25, 26, 27, 28, 4, 5]

The hidden portal to Jigran

During his confinement, Yam-Akara gains access to the governor’s library. Old exploration reports reveal that the powerful “artifact” is a forgotten passage to another land. Trickster offers a key to the gate, then sends Kir on a fruitless ore search so that he can work without interference. With the key ready, Yam-Akara warns that he cannot sense the destination: the portal may be defective or concealed by a powerful absorbing spell. Kir recognises the same absence Tka-Rik described and concludes that it leads to Jigran. He decides to go directly, trusting the strength gained during his journey. Kel chooses to accompany him again. [5, 29, 30, 31]
